description: Hankinnan kohteena ovat sairaalasänkyjen, sairaalakalusteiden sekä lääkekaappien hankinnat Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialueelle tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisin ehdoin. Hankinta on jaettu kuuteen (6) osa-alueeseen: Osa-alue 1. Sairaalasängyt ja potilaspöydät Osa-alue 2. Tutkimus- ja toimenpidepöydät Osa-alue 3. Lääkekaapit ja lääkejääkaapit Osa-alue 4. Muut sairaalakalusteet ja tarvikkeet Osa-alue 5. Gynekologiset tutkimuspöydät Osa-alue 6. Vaunut ja logistiikkakalusteet Tarjoaja voi tarjota yhteen tai useampaan osa-alueeseen. Hankinnassa muodostetaan osa-aluekohtaisesti puitejärjestely, johon valitaan kaksi (2) Toimittajaa per osa-alue, mikäli tarjouspyynnön ehdot täyttäviä tarjouksia on saatu vähintään ilmoitettu määrä. Toimittajat asetetaan osa-aluekohtaisesti kokonaistaloudellisen edullisuuden perusteella etusijajärjestykseen. Osa-alueissa 2, 4 ja 6, mikäli osa-aluekohtaisesti kahden etusijajärjestyksessä parhaiten sijoittuneen tarjoajan tuotetarjonnat eivät yhdessä kata kaikkia kyseisen osa-alueen tarjouspyynnössä määriteltyjä tuotepositioita, hankintayksikkö valitsee osa-aluekohtaiseen puitejärjestelyyn myös kolmanneksi sijoittuneen tarjouspyynnön ehdot täyttäneen tarjoajan tarjouksen tuotepositioiden saatavuuden varmistamiseksi. Osa-alueeseen valitaan kuitenkin enintään kolme (3) toimittajaa. Sopimuskausi on määräaikaisena voimassa kaksi (2) vuotta. Tavoitteena on, että sopimuskausi alkaa 1.1.2027. Osa-aluekohtaiseen puitesopimukseen sisältyy optiona puitesopimuksen jatkaminen enintään kahdella (2) vuodella. Tilaaja ilmoittaa option käytöstä kirjallisesti viimeistään kolme (3) kuukautta ennen varsinaisen sopimuskauden päättymistä. Option käyttö on yksin Tilaajan harkinnassa. Sopimusehdot ovat optiokaudella tämän puitesopimuksen mukaiset. Hankinnan ennakoitu kokonaisarvo neljän (4) vuoden sopimuskaudelle on noin 900 000 - 1,1 miljoonaa euroa (alv 0 %). Enimmäiskokonaisarvo on määritetty siten, että se kattaa mahdolliset käyttömäärien vaihtelut koko sopimuskauden aikana. Ennakoitu arvo on hankintayksikön arvio, eikä se muodosta hankintayksikölle ostovelvoitetta. Puitejärjestely ei sisällä ostovelvoitetta, eikä hankintayksikkö sitoudu hankkimaan tuotteita enimmäiskokonaisarvoon asti.

title: Call for Solutions - DeCA Stuttgart Area Commissaries Facility Maintenance
description: The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is seeking innovative, commercial approaches for commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) maintenance services for the commissaries within the Stuttgart (Kelley, Patch, Panzer and Robinson) area. The prospective contractor shall provide a comprehensive preventative, unscheduled, and 24/7/365 emergency maintenance for commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) services to ensure continuous operations and prevent inventory loss. Solutions should demonstrate rapid on-site emergency response capabilities, preventative maintenance compliant with local commercial standards, transparent fixed-price quoting and reporting procedures, and full compliance with applicable host nation (German/EU) statutory requirements and Department of War (DoW) statutory, safety, and warranty standards from firms operating in European Union, compliant with EU and host nation specific regulations and standards as it relates to commercial Facility and Equipment (FM) preventive maintenance and repair. Attached documents contain technical data that will provide assistance in understanding current conditions that the commercial solution will need to meet. Our objective is to establish a long term partnership with a provider whose technology, service model, and commercial terms align with our commitment to delivering reliable, value driven solutions. DeCA seeks solutions that will provide this support for up to five total years, requesting that solutions propose a Period of Performance (PoP) that reflect customary commercial lead times, development lifecycles, use of CAFM systems, and repair benchmarks for the proposed support. The Government reserves the right to adjust the proposed PoP to align with mission requirements, funding availability, and applicable regulatory limitations, including structuring the award as a base period with one or more option periods at the Government's discretion. Please download the PDF documents attached to this call for solutions for additional details. title: Service Contract Renewal OXFORD INSTRUMENTS
description: NOTICE OF INTENT � SOLE-SOURCE ACQUISITION Notice No.: 75N98027Q00045 The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD), intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Oxford Instruments (Witec Instruments) for Service Contract for WiTec Raman Microscope Systems, Model: Alpha 300+, Serial No. 100-1200-2268. Description of the Requirement Service contract is essential for preventive maintenance, calibration and timely repairs of Witec Alpha 300R Raman microscope. Oxford Instruments Inc. (formerly known as Witec Instruments Inc) is the sole provider of genuine spare parts for these instruments and only qualified Oxford Instruments technicians can perform maintenance and repair of the equipment. A contract with a third-party repair/maintenance service will void Oxford service contract, and significantly increase the risk of disruptions in SPB/NICHD/NIH mission in the case of serious instrument failure. Contractor shall perform the following: PM � 1 Annual Preventative Maintenance (and/or Calibration) on-site Field Service Engineer Visit � covers PM parts, labor, travel expense. TECHNICAL SUPPORT �Access to Helpdesk and Technical Support included with priority response time during standard business hours Monday-Friday 8:30AM-5PM EST, excluding Federal Holidays. Technical Remote Support subject to connectivity and availability. LABOUR: Labor and Travel Expenses for all on-site FSE visits are included. PARTS � Includes replacement parts CONSUMABLES: consumables are not covered -however, a 10% OFF SILVER Contract discount applies towards all consumables via Oxford Instruments Online Store, Link to eStore: https://estore.oxinst.com/us SOFTWARE: Software fault or bug fixes are included. Software Updates are also included. Contractor shall provide OEM certified parts for all preventative maintenance and service repairs, except for consumables, at no additional cost to the Government. Shipping and handling parts under warranty or contract shall not be charged to the Government. Contractor shall provide an OEM service technician to perform all preventive maintenance inspections, service repairs and technical support. Justification for the Proposed Sole-Source Acquisition The Government intends to solicit from a single source pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Oxford Instruments Inc. is the manufacturer of the WTIec alpha300R Raman microscope and the sole provider of alignment and maintenance services currently deployed at the SPB / NICHD. As the manufacturer, Oxford Instruments maintains the proprietary hardware, firmware configurations, calibration specifications, replacement parts inventory required to support the WTIec alpha300R microscope. The WTIec alpha300R system, including its hardware, software, firmware, calibration and alignment processes, and supporting documentation, is proprietary to Oxford Instruments Inc. Maintenance services must be performed using manufacturer-approved procedures and replacement components to preserve compatibility with the existing hardware and software, and retain manufacturer support. To the Government's knowledge, no other vendor possesses the proprietary technology, replacement components, or integrated calibration/alignment capabilities necessary to provide maintenance services that are fully compatible with the existing WTIec alpha300R Raman microscope. Response Information This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required preventive maintenance and remedial repair services for the specified instrument and meet all applicable technical and operational requirements. The Government will review timely submissions to determine whether another responsible source is capable of satisfying the requirement and whether a competitive acquisition is appropriate. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source can satisfy the requirement. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to Verne.Griffin@nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on November 9, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98027Q00045 in the subject line of the submission.

title: Quantitative Analysis of Longitudinal MR Images
description: See attached Sources Sought Notice and attached Draft Statement of Work. SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Solicitation Number: 75N98027R00005 Title: Quantitative Analysis of Longitudinal MR Images Classification Code/Title: AN11 - Health R&D Services; Health Care Services; Basic Research NAICS Code/Title: 541714 Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology) Size Standard: 1,000 employees Description: This is a Research and Development (R & D) Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential R & D requirement. This notice is issued to help determine the availability of qualified companies technically capable of meeting the Government requirement and to determine the method of acquisition. It is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Small businesses are encouraged to respond. Background: Since 1958, the Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Aging (BLSA) has been a major research program conducted by the National Institute on Aging (NIA). The BLSA is a multi-disciplinary study of physiologic and psychological aspects of normal aging in community-dwelling men and women. Active BLSA participants are volunteers who visit the Clinical Unit of the NIA-Intramural Research Program (IRP) in Baltimore, MD for testing every 1 to 4 years. Since 1994, the NIA has been conducting a longitudinal brain imaging study of older adults in the BLSA to characterize individual differences in longitudinal brain changes, to investigate the extent to which these brain changes underlie individual differences in cognitive aging, to identify brain changes that may be predictors of cognitive decline and Alzheimer�s disease, and to assess the impact of potential modulators of brain and cognitive aging. As of October, 2024, more than 4000 neuroimaging evaluations have been performed for BLSA participants. As part of this research program, it has also been necessary to develop and validate sophisticated tools for analysis of longitudinal neuroimaging data that can be applied in large-scale studies. Thus, this project has involved the development, validation, and refinement of novel image analysis tools and the application of these tools to longitudinal Magnetic Resonance (MR) imaging scans and Positron Emission Tomography (PET) measures of regional cerebral blood flow, amyloid and tau deposition in brain. More recently, these tools include advanced machine learning approaches using pattern analysis to classify clinical status and aging trajectories of individuals based on structural and functional brain images. The work of this requirement will continue to focus on the application of sophisticated tools and quantitative analysis of longitudinal MRI data acquired from BLSA participants. Thus, the proposed contract will apply methods developed in prior acquisitions, that allow continuity of research and provide longitudinal consistency of measures of global and regional brain volumes and ischemic lesion volumes, as well as functional MR data, including consistency with MR data acquired during earlier phases of this project (since 1994). This Contract will also require the application of sophisticated analytic approaches, including previously developed machine learning and pattern analysis methods, to allow classification of risk for cognitive impairment and likelihood of maintenance of cognitive resiience on an individual subject basis. Purpose and Objectives: The principal goal of this procurement is to provide quantification of MR imaging scans to provide measures of brain structure and function in BLSA participants, including heterogenous brain aging trajectories. Specifically, these data will allow NIA investigators to continue to address the following questions: What are the rates and regional distribution of changes in brain anatomy in non-demented men and women throughout adulthood? What is the frequency and progression of brain abnormalities in older adults and what is the clinical significance of these findings for cognitive aging? Against a background of age-related changes in brain structure, which changes predict cognitive impairment and Alzheimer�s disease, and conversely, what are the predictors of the maintenance of cognitive health or cognitive resilience? What factors modulate cognitive and brain aging and how do they impact brain-behavior associations? Project Requirements: See attached Draft Statement of Work. Anticipated Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is one year from date of award. Capability Statement/Information Sought: Companies that believe they possess the capabilities to provide the required products should submit documentation of their ability to meet each of the project requirements to the Contracting Officer. The capability statement must specifically address each of the project requirements separately. Additionally, the capability statement should include 1) the total number of employees, 2) the professional qualifications of personnel as it relates to the requirements outlined, 3) any contractor GSA Schedule contracts and/or other government-wide acquisition contracts (GWACs) by which all of the requirements may be met, if applicable, and 4) any other information considered relevant to this program. Capability statements must also include the Company Name, Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov, Physical Address, and Point of Contact Information. The response must include the respondents� technical and administrative points of contact, including names, titles, addresses, telephone and fax numbers, and e-mail addresses. Interested companies are required to identify their type of business, applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code, and size standards in accordance with the Small Business Administration. The government requests that no proprietary or confidential business data be submitted in a response to this notice. However, responses that indicate the information therein is proprietary will be properly safeguarded for Government use only. Capability statements must include the name and telephone number of a point of contact having authority and knowledge to discuss responses with Government representatives. Capability statements in response to this market survey that do not provide sufficient information for evaluation will be considered non-responsive. When submitting this information, please reference the solicitation notice number. One (1) copy of the response is required and must be in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format using 11-point or 12-point font, 8-1/2� x 11� paper size, with 1� top, bottom, left and right margins, and with single or double spacing. The information submitted must be in and outline format that addresses each of the elements of the project requirement and in the capability statement /information sought paragraphs stated herein. A cover page and an executive summary may be included but is not required. The response is limited to ten (10) page limit. The 10-page limit does not include the cover page, executive summary, or references, if requested. description: Description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police in Iqaluit, Nunavut Territories, has a requirement for Generator Inspection & Maintenance Services at the RCMP Cambridge Bay, Clyde River, Gjoa Haven, Kinngait, Qikitarjuaq, Taloyoak Detachments, Iqaluit Headquarters Building and Iqaluit Hangar. This procurement is subject to the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement and the Directive on Government Contracts, Including Real Property Leases, in the Nunavut Settlement Area. Bidders are requested to maximize Inuit employment, subcontracting and on-the-job training opportunities, and involve Inuit businesses, in carrying out the work under this project. The Nunavut Agreement contains a provision requiring the inclusion of socio-economic bid criteria in the solicitation document, when practicable and consistent with sound procurement management principles. These socio-economic bid criteria are referred to as Nunavut Benefits Criteria (NBC) and Inuit Benefits Criteria (IBC), and bidders propose Inuit benefits in their bid submission via an Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP). This solicitation is limited for bidding among firms registered on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). Bids submitted by businesses not on the IFR will render the bid non-responsive and no further consideration will be accorded to the bid. Delivery Date: The contract period will be for 36-months from the date of contract, with the option to extend for 2 additional 1 year periods. Security: This requirement contains a security requirement. Basis of selection: A bid must comply with all the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory requirements. Bids not meeting the requirements will be declared non-responsive. The selection will be based on the highest responsive combined rating of total Inuit Benefits Plan (IBP) merit, and price. The ratio will be 30% for the total IBP merit, and 70% for price. Tenders must be submitted to the RCMP Bid Receiving Unit at: NWR_Procurement_Bids@rcmp-grc.gc.ca Refer to the attached tender documents to obtain further information. Canada retains the right to negotiate with any supplier on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. The RCMP has adopted the Integrity Regime administered by Public Services and Procurement Canada. As a result, the integrity provisions are being applied in RCMP contracting activities as outlined in this solicitation. Canada will make available Notices of Proposed Procurement (NPP), bid solicitations and related documents for download through the Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) at https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities . Canada is not responsible and will not assume any liabilities whatsoever for the information found on websites of third parties. In the event an NPP, bid solicitation or related documentation would be amended, Canada will not be sending notifications. Canada will post all amendments, including significant enquiries received and their replies, using GETS. It is the sole responsibility of the Bidder to regularly consult GETS for the most up-to-date information. Canada will not be liable for any oversight on the Bidder's part nor for notification services offered by a third party. Having a business profile in the IBD will increase your company’s visibility and may provide additional business. title: Netherlands – Marine survey services – Raamovereenkomst Vooronderzoeken Baggeren Lansingerland
description: Baggerwerkzaamheden maken onderdeel uit van het reguliere beheer en onderhoud van de watergangen binnen de gemeente Lansingerland en vormen daarmee een periodiek terugkerende activiteit. Om de benodigde baggerwerkzaamheden planmatig en doelmatig te kunnen voorbereiden, dient periodiek te worden vastgesteld welke watergangen in aanmerking komen voor uitvoering in de daaropvolgende jaren. De gemeente is voornemens een raamovereenkomst af te sluiten voor het uitvoeren van de benodigde vooronderzoeken en toezicht op baggeren. Deze vooronderzoeken omvatten onder meer het bepalen van het te baggeren areaal, het uitvoeren van waterbodem- en ecologische onderzoeken en overige onderzoeken die noodzakelijk zijn voor de voorbereiding van baggerwerken. De resultaten van deze onderzoeken vormen de basis voor het samenstellen van uitvoerbare werkpakketten voor de reeds gecontracteerde baggeraar. De verwachte omzet voor vier jaar bedraagt € 380.000,-. Het Plafondbedrag van de raamovereenkomst voor vier jaar bedraagt € 494.000,-.

title: Firefox
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has developed a non-invasive coherent optical system capable of recording neural signals in humans. To expand this foundational technology and enable the development of revolutionary, non-invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), DARPA's Firefox program is soliciting approaches to overcome key technological hurdles: 1) development of components enabling dynamic rastering/scanning of the incoming coherent optical signal to target multiple regions of interest and 2) development of new data processing architectures beyond the digital domain to handle the high data rates and computational burden inherent to scaling the amount of neural data recorded by the optical system. The ultimate goal of the Firefox program is to use these innovations to develop a 100-channel, non-invasive BCI with 50-micron spatial and 100-microsecond temporal resolution.

title: Painting and Maintenance Services in Apartments for the U.S. Mission in Paris, France
description: The Embassy of the United States in Paris, France, will release a solicitation for Painting and Maintenance Services in Apartments Leased in Paris and its vicinity by the Embassy of the United States in France. title: FY27 USAFE A3ZJ ADSi Software License Renewal
description: SOLICITATION NOTICE: The 700th Contracting Squadron (700 CONS) intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price purchase order to Ultra Electronics Advanced Tactical Systems, Inc. (UEI: HMT9NXXLZGP9). The purchase order will provide a 12-month renewal of Air Defense Systems Integrator (ADSI) software licenses and associated maintenance for the Scalable Control Reporting Agile Mission�Kit (SCRAM-K). This renewal will support the continued use of SCRAM-K by both USAFE-AFAFRICA A3ZJ and the 606th Air Control Squadron (606 ACS). The anticipated award date is 11 November 2026. ADSI is a specialized Government software that supports mission training, exercises, and operational requirements. The renewal will maintain continued software availability, compatibility, vendor updates, and technical support for authorized users. The renewal supports USAFE A3ZJ and the 606th Air Control Squadron (606 ACS) by maintaining access to existing ADSI software, vendor updates, security patches, and technical support. This renewal is required to sustain authorized use of the ADSI software and maintain access to manufacturer-provided maintenance services. Award to Ultra Electronics Advanced Tactical Systems, Inc. will ensure continuity of licensing, product support, and routine software maintenance without interruption to mission support activities. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes. However interested parties may submit a capability statement upon the referenced deadline within the attached solicitation (FA561327Q0004) demonstrating their ability to perform the requirement described herein. title: Solicitation - BWT Operation and Maintenance
description: SOLICITATION - OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE OF GOVERNMENT-OWNED FACILITIES AND EQUIPMENT, BLACK WARRIOR- TOMBIGBEE AND ALABAMA RIVER WATERWAYS PROJECT FACILITIES, ALABAMA - Furnish all planning, supervision, administration, labor, equipment, material, supplies, replacement or repair parts, and all things necessary for the Operations and Maintenance of Government-Owned Facilities and Equipment, Black Warrior- Tombigbee and Alabama River Waterways Project Facilities, Alabama. The project is geographically spread out over 13 counties in Alabama: Washington, Clarke, Marengo, Choctaw, Sumter, Hale, Greene, Tuscaloosa, Monroe, Wilcox, Dallas, Lowndes, and Autauga Counties, on the Black Warrior and Tombigbee BWT River System and the Alabama River System. The Project Management Office has responsibility for the operation and maintenance of nine locks and dams, two resource offices, a Project Management Office, two boat houses, one boat storage facility, storage buildings, two contractor maintenance compounds, and two hydro-electric generating plants. The BWT/AL Project is home to 9 beautiful lakes, they include Bankhead, Holt, Oliver, Warrior, Demopolis, Coffeeville, Claiborne, Millers, and RF Henry. These lakes for the BWT stretch from the headwaters near Birmingham, AL, south through Tuscaloosa and Demopolis to the southernmost Mobile District Corps facility located below Coffeeville, and for the AL river south from Montgomery, AL to the confluence with the Tombigbee River. The project is operated under the direction of Mobile District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile, Alabama. It is anticipated that one 1 Firm-Fixed Price FFP, Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity IDIQ, Single Award Task Order Contract SATOC will be awarded for a five 5-year ordering period. In general, not all inclusive, services to be performed include general maintenance, cleaning, custodial service, garbage removal, grass mowing, saddle dike and overlook clearing, debris removal, clerical duties at a Resource Office, repair to riprap slopes, repair to earthen slopes, excavation, and storage and disposal of hazardous and-or toxic materials, such as herbicides and waste fluids from vehicle maintenance. The IDIQ performance work statement PWS will include, but is not limited to, the following types of work: maintenance and repair of locks, dams, levees, riprap-concrete structures, flow structures, buildings, offices, maintenance facilities, operation areas, project roads, vehicles, floating plant, boathouses, bathhouses, washhouses, toilets, gatehouses, security and other fences, sanitary disposal systems, small boat launching ramps, playground equipment, bulletin boards, game courts, water and electrical systems, telephone lines, picnic sites, campsites, and other related facilities. Tasks required to perform this type of maintenance include carpentry, masonry, electrical, electronics, mechanical, structural, plumbing, chipping, caulking, sealing, cleaning, welding and replacing parts of or full pieces of equipment. Additional maintenance work includes guardrails, gates, electric barrier gates, signs, bumper blocks, landscaped areas, beaches, navigation or swimming buoys, paved roads, parking lots, trails, navigation aids, courtesy docks, and boundary lines. Operational requirements encompass the maintenance of a specialized floating plant comprising a primary towboat, crane barge, and auxiliary workboats and barges to support the Black Warrior-Tombigbee BWT and Alabama River Systems. This area of responsibility AOR extends from the mouth of the Mobile River to Birmingham on the BWT system and to Montgomery on the Alabama River system. These multi-purpose civil works projects are vital to facilitating commercial navigation, supporting public recreation, and managing regional wildlife habitats. This procurement is 100% set-aside for small business. title: Laboratory Support Services
description: The Defense Prisoner of War/Missing in Action Accounting Agency (DPAA) conducts global research, investigation, recovery, and laboratory operations to identify and account for unaccounted-for Department of Defense (DoD) personnel from past conflicts. These efforts support the DoD personnel accounting mission. DPAA was established on January 30, 2015; however, its predecessor organizations have supported the personnel accounting mission for decades. DPAA operates a satellite laboratory at Offutt Air Force Base, Nebraska, which opened in June 2013. DPAA also maintains permanent detachments that support host-nation access, logistics, and in-country requirements for investigation and recovery operations. These detachments include Detachment 1 in Bangkok, Thailand; Detachment 2 in Hanoi, Vietnam; Detachment 3 in Vientiane, Laos; and Detachment Europe in Miesau, Germany. DPAA Scientific Analysis (SA), also referred to as the DPAA laboratory, is a large and diverse forensic skeletal laboratory staffed by forensic anthropologists, archaeologists, and odontologists. The laboratory performs scientific analysis to support the identification of missing personnel. In 2003, the laboratory became the second Federal laboratory to achieve accreditation under the American Society of Crime Laboratory Directors/Laboratory Accreditation Board (ASCLD/LAB) International Standards Program. Laboratory accreditation supports the DoD Defense Forensic Enterprise program and is consistent with DoD Directive 5110.10, Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA). DPAA regional directorates, including the Indo-Pacific (IP) Directorate and Europe-Mediterranean (EM) Directorate, conduct complex historical research and archaeological analysis in support of recovery, investigation, and disinterment missions. The regional directorates plan and execute field investigations and recovery operations worldwide. The Partnerships and Innovations Directorate supports these global field operations. This contract supports DPAA laboratory and regional-directorate requirements necessary to advance the Agency�s mission of accounting for as many missing service members as feasible each year. DPAA�s planning objective is to maintain the capacity and capability to account for 200 or more individuals annually.

title: Marine Corps Education Command Information Technology Support Services
description: The Marine Corps Installations Command National Capital Region - Regional Contracting Office (MCINCR-RCO), Quantico, VA, has a requirement for Information Technology Support Services for the United States Marine Corps Education Command (EDCOM). The Government intends to issue a single award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract, consisting of Firm Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract Line Items for services and Cost Reimbursement (CR) for travel. The contract will have a five-year ordering period, totaling $45M ceiling value. The proposed acquisition is done as a 100% set aside to Women Owned Small Business. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541512. The Government is soliciting proposals utilizing commercial contracting under FAR Part 12 and FAR 15- Contracting by Negotiation. The Government intends to award a contract using best value trade-off procedures. The award will be issued on an all or none basis. This procurement is being solicited under solicitation M00264-27-R-0001, which is posted via the Solicitation Module in the Procurement Integration Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website (https://piee.eb.mil). It is the responsibility of the offeror to continually view the website for the solicitation and any amendments. Contractors interested in doing business with the Government must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) website accessed through https://www.sam.gov. Contractor must also ensure annual representations and certifications are current or complete them at the SAM website as well. All prospective offerors interested in submitting an offer must have a commercial and government entity code (CAGE code). The points of contact for this solicitation are Genia Fouts, Contract Specialist at genia.fouts@usmc.mil, Jeffrey A. Sisk Sr. Team Lead at jeffrey.a.sisk@usmc.mil, and Christian Hernandez, Contracting Officer at christian.hernandezsoto@usmc.mil. All responsible sources may submit a proposal for consideration upon solicitation release. NOTE: The pre-solicitation of this requirement was posted in SAM.GOV under related notice RFI M00264-26-RFI-0028. Please note that a new RFP number has been used due to posting in FY2027. The prior referenced RFP no. M00264-26-R-0015 is no longer in use.

title: Comprehensive full-service maintenance/repair plan for Vitek 2 Compact 60
description: The United States Department of the Navy Medicine Research and Development Command (NMRDC) intends to award a sole source contract to, bioMerieux, Inc, Salt Lake City, UT 84108. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals however If interested Government shall consider all responses. The Genomics and Bioinformatics Department of the Biological Defense Research Directorate, NMRDC-Frederick maintains a state-of-the-art genomics and bioinformatics research program. As part of their ongoing efforts to diminish the burden that increased antimicrobial resistance pose for the health of our military, the Vitek 2 Compact system will be used to characterize the antibiotic resistance profiles of pathogenic bacteria isolated from clinically relevant enteric samples and compare those phenotypic data to the genes detected via sequencing. Without proper service agreements, mission critical scientific research may be compromised. This instrument is a delicate, specialized, highly technical, state-of-the-art laboratory instrument that must receive preventative maintenance and periodic updates in accordance with the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) standards/procedures by certified, authorized technicians, and be covered by a comprehensive maintenance/repair support plan/agreement in the case of hardware malfunction/failure. The need is for a Comprehensive full-service maintenance/repair plan for a Vitek 2 Compact 60. One year support plan must include at a minimum: Full coverage for OEM parts and labor/travel for OEM certified and authorized service technicians. One on-site preventative maintenance (PM) visit done IAW OEM standards/requirements by OEM certified and authorized service technician(s). Remote technical support from OEM certified and authorized service technician(s). This support is provided 24 hours a day / 7 days a week. On-site response by OEM certified and authorized service technician(s) within 24 hours of an issue with the hardware�s performance using commercially reasonable efforts. The NAICS code for this action is 811210. This requirement will be procured under the guidelines of FAR Part 12 Commercial Items. NMRDC requires that all contractors doing business with the Acquisition Office must be registered with the Systems for Award Management (SAM). No award can be made unless the vendor is registered in Systems for Award Management. For additional information and to register in SAM, please access the following website: https://www.sam.gov/. In order to register with the SAM and to be eligible to receive an award from this Acquisition Office, all offers must have a Unique Entity Identification Number (UEI). A Sam.gov number may be acquired free of charge by contacting Sam.gov online at www.sam.gov or by phone at (866) 606-8220.

Tarjottaviin hintoihin tulee sisällyttää kaikki palvelun tuottamisesta tulevat kulut, jotka sisältävät mahdolliset kilometri, matka-, majoitus-, päiväraha-, ylityö- sekä toimitus-, laskutus- ja toimistokulut, työkalut, jätemaksut ja pientarvikelisät mukaan lukien. Hankinta toteutetaan puitejärjestelynä etusijajärjestyksessä. Hankinta ei koske takuuhuoltoja, huuhteluautoja eikä Oulun kaupungin leasing-kalustoa. title: Granite Surface Plate Calibration and lapping - with Q&As
description: Q&A's: 1. CLINs 0001 through 0005 (pages 3-5) are each one firm-fixed-price lot for "Inspection and calibration." SOW paragraphs 1 and 4.2 (pages 1-2) call for lapping only of plates that are out of specification, the QASP (Attachment 0002, page 1) says lapping repairs must be authorized by the CO or COR, and Section G, paragraph 6.a (page 12) asks for labor rates. Should each year's lot price cover inspection and calibration of all 18 plates, with lapping priced separately (for example, a per-plate price or an hourly labor rate) and billed only when authorized? Or should the lot price include all lapping that may be needed that year? If lapping is priced separately, where in the quote should those prices or rates be shown? Answer: Firm fixed for calibration of all plates listed in the SOW. Lapping to be priced separately. We don�t know which plates will require lapping or how much lapping per plate will be needed. We are asking for an hourly rate for lapping. Whether the plate is big or small, the hourly rate would be the same. Plates may require a lot of lapping or very little. Pricing lapping by the plate doesn�t seem to make much sense. 2. Each CLIN (pages 3-5) states "All travel shall be in accordance with the Joint Travel Regulation (JTR)," and SOW paragraph 2 (page 1) says invoices will be checked against the contract prices and JTR approved prices. Should travel be included in each year's firm-fixed lot price, or will it be reimbursed separately at JTR rates? If it is reimbursed separately, how should travel be shown in the quote? Answer: Include estimated travel costs in the firm-fixed pricing. The Vendor that gets the award will bill actual costs after the service. 3. Section G, paragraph 6.c (page 12) asks offerors to "concur at the bottom of the Scope of Work (SOW) and sign," but Attachment 0001 ends at paragraph 15.1 on page 4 with no concurrence or signature block. Is it acceptable to add a signed and dated concurrence statement at the bottom of SOW page 4, or to submit a separate signed concurrence page on company letterhead that references Attachment 0001 dated 15 Oct 26? Answer: Either is fine by me. _______________________ All Vendors MUST submit all requirements plus the signed Soliciation to the POC before the closing date and time or they will not be considered for this action.

description: 657-27-103JB, FCA Replace Building 51 Roof This is a Sources Sought Notice to determine the availability of service disabled veteran owned small business (SDVOSB) firms for a possible small business category type set-aside for Construction Services project: This is a Sources Sought Notice that is issued for information and planning purposes only and is not to be construed as a commitment� by the government, implied or otherwise to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract.� An award will not be made on information received in response to this notice.� This notice is not a Request for Proposal (RFP); it is a market research tool being utilized to determine the availability of sources prior to issuing a Best Value type RFP. PROJECT DESCRIPTION AND SCOPE 1. This contract is for CONSTRUCTION services for the work required to replace the existing roof and associated components on Building 51 at the St. Louis Medical Center Jefferson Barracks. 2. Description: Construction services: Furnish complete construction services to replace all designated Building 51 roofs, including projections, entrance roofs, and connecting portions. The preliminary net roof area is approximately 56,000 square feet, subject to field verification. Provide a watertight thermoplastic polyolefin (TPO) roofing system in accordance with the VA-prepared drawings and specifications. Contractor shall submit shop drawings, product data, and installation details for all proposed materials, equipment, and systems to be installed or replaced under this contract for VA review prior to commencing the associated work. Submittals shall include applicable manufacturer's specifications and required engineering certifications. Schedule, phasing, and occupied operations: Complete construction and closeout within 222 calendar days after the Notice to Proceed issue date. Building 51 remains occupied and operational 24 hours per day, seven days per week. Work hours are from 7:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., local time. Submit a contractor-developed phasing plan for the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) to review before roofing. Complete both highest penthouse roof platforms first on the original building and the highest roof section first on the addition; either building portion may be started first. Maintain safe access, utilities, and required infection-control and HVAC-intake protection. Provide construction fall protection and keep the building watertight; coordinate service interruptions with the VA. Investigation and Roofing Requirements: a. Hazardous Materials: While neither Asbestos Containing Material nor Lead is expected to be encountered within the scope of this project, it will be the responsibility of the contractor to hire an independent 3rd party VPIH to complete the related work if they are to encounter a material that they deem suspicious. b. Demolition limit: At the original building (Zones 1-7, 13, and 14), remove the existing roofing assembly through the base sheet to the top of the Zonolite lightweight-concrete topping; retain the topping and underlying structural concrete deck. At the addition (Zones 8-12 and 15), remove the existing roofing assembly, including insulation and intervening layers, to the top of the metal roof deck; retain the deck and supporting structure. Clean and inspect retained surfaces, and repair deterioration within specified repair limits. Report differing construction or deterioration beyond those limits to the COR before proceeding with affected work. c. New roof and mechanical securement: Install mechanically fastened rigid insulation, adhered cover board, and fully adhered 70-mil TPO roofing membrane with continuous hot-airwelded seams. Contractor shall verify that the proposed fastening system is compatible with Building 51's existing roof construction. d. Parapets, penetrations, and retained metal: Extend new roofing up parapets to the existing flashing. Flash and seal, with the correct system specific boots, all roof penetrations with compatible membrane extending at least 8 inches above the finished roof, or higher where required by applicable VA criteria and manufacturer/warranty requirements. Retain metal flashings, flanges, and coping unless scheduled for replacement, and replace roofing beneath retained metal. Specific Replacement and Repairs: e. Associated roof work: Retain rooftop HVAC units in place and replace roofing beneath elevated units and frames and around curbs. Replace old or deteriorated wooden rooftop support blocks with load-rated black rubber blocks compatible with the roofing; retain serviceable recently replaced blocks. Replace roof-drain covers/strainers and recondition retained drains with watertight connections. Reflash existing scuppers and provide new scuppers only where detailed; retain gutters and downspouts unless otherwise indicated. Correct approximately 250 square feet of depressed roof on the original building's middle section north of the penthouse to provide positive drainage. Replace expansion-joint weatherproofing/cover material at two original-building sections, approximately 40 linear feet each. Temporarily remove and reinstall the existing lightning-protection system in its original locations and configuration with new clips securing it; complete specified testing and certification. Repair approximately 150 linear feet of the existing movable stanchion-andrope warning-line barrier. Replace the penthouse roof-access ladder to meet applicable VA safety requirements and OSHA criteria. Install 3-foot by 3-foot walking pads with 8-inch clear gaps along approximately 600 linear feet of total walkway route, including gaps. Provide positive drainage to roof drains and scuppers throughout all reroofed areas. Standing water shall not remain more than 48 hours after rainfall ends under conditions conducive to drying. Correct low spots and other drainage deficiencies that prevent compliance before final acceptance. f. Skylights: Replace four skylights: two approximately 85 square feet each and two approximately 40 square feet each. Field-verify openings and provide complete watertight installations. Before fabrication, submit contractor shop drawings and supporting structural calculations signed and sealed by a licensed structural engineer responsible for their design/review. g. Submittals, record drawings, and closeout: Provide required construction submittals and complete specified testing, inspections, and closeout. Submit a clean, coordinated as-built record drawing set in searchable PDF and editable CAD showing actual installed conditions and accepted changes; redline markups alone are not acceptable. Provide a 20-year nodollar-limit (NDL) warranty and maintenance information, complete cleanup and restoration, and comply with contract records-management, privacy, and security requirements. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the estimated magnitude of the resulting construction price range is estimated to be between $2,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. Request For Proposal (RFP) for Pharmacological testing of novel stimulants, and synthetic cannabinoids.
description: Amended Request For Proposal (RFP) for Pharmacological testing of stimulants, and synthetic cannabinoids. Novel psychoactive substances (NPS) in the illegal drug supply pose risks to Canadians. However, little is known about their pharmacological activity. More potent drugs increase the risk of overdose risks. Evidence on the pharmacological activity of these substances is essential to support scientific regulatory activities and risk assessments. The illegal drug supply is continuously evolving, with new substances continually being detected. There is a need for further information on their harms to Canadians. This procurement activity will allow for the evaluation of the in vitro pharmacological activity of two categories of emerging drugs: synthetic cannabinoids, and stimulants. The data generated from this contract will inform future assessment activities and allow the OLRA to make more informed regulatory science decisions. For both streams, they require the pharmacological testing of different classes of substances, and require acquisition of reference standards and control samples, getting licenses for controlled substances, conducting experiments (including doing statistical analysis), and finally drafting and finalizing reports. Canada is seeking offers from Offerors to provide Pharmacological Testing for Stimulants, and Synthetic Cannabinoids in two (2) separate streams to Health Canada. Stream 2 – In vitro pharmacological testing of novel synthetic cannabinoids and Stream 3 – In vitro pharmacological testing of stimulant compounds. Each stream will be evaluated separately, and bidders are to provide their submissions for one (1) stream or two (2) streams. Up to two (2) contracts may be awarded under this amended request for proposal.

description: 35,000# Base Capacity 4-Wheel Sit-Down AC Electric Lift TruckHeavy-Capacity Battery-Electric ForkliftQuantity: 1 eachDelivery Location: McAlester Army Ammunition Plant Warehouse 8 C Tree RdMcAlester, OK 74501Required Delivery Date: Before or No Later Than September 30th, 2027.Delivery Terms: FOB Destination.1. RequirementThe Government requires the purchase and delivery of quantity 1 each, new heavy-capacity, battery-electric, counterbalanced forklift(s) for indoor industrial material-handling operations.The offered equipment shall be new, current production, and meet or exceed every minimum salient characteristic below. Used, refurbished, remanufactured, prototype, or demonstrator equipment is not acceptable.A manufacturer name, brand, or model number is not required. Offerors may propose any make or model that meets all stated requirements.2. Minimum Salient CharacteristicsCharacteristic. Minimum Requirement2.1 Equipment type. Four-wheel, sit-down, counterbalanced, battery-electric forklift suitable for heavy industrial material handling. AC Drive and Lift System.2.2 Electrical system. Battery-electric propulsion and lift system. The system shall provide performance equal to or better than a 72-volt electrical system. Shall have transistor control technology.2.3 Rated capacity. The forklift shall have a rated lifting capacity of not less than 28,700 pounds at a 24-inch load center and at a maximum fork height of 103.5 inches, with the furnished forks and fork-positioner attachment installed. Free Lift 0.0 inches with standard Load Backrest.2.4 Capacity data plate. The delivered forklift shall have a legible manufacturer capacity/data plate identifying the rated capacity for the furnished mast, forks, and attachment configuration.2.5 Mast. Two-stage mast, or functionally equivalent high visibility heavy duty mast rails configuration, capable of a maximum fork height of not less than 103.5 inches.2.6 Lowered mast height Overall lowered mast height shall not exceed 112.7 inches.2.7 Overhead guard height. Overhead guard height shall not exceed 102.56 inches.2.8 Mast tilt. Mast shall provide at least 6 degrees forward tilt and 7 degrees rearward tilt.2.9 Carriage. Pin-type carriage, or functionally equivalent carriage, compatible with the furnished fork positioner. Nominal carriage width shall be 62 inches.2.10 Forks. Furnish one pair of forks with minimum dimensions of 3.5 inches thick x 7 inches wide x 72 inches long. Forks shall be compatible with the furnished carriage and rated for the forklift/attachment configuration.2.11 Fork positioner. Furnish an integral sideshifting fork positioner Pin Type (includes 4-way Valve and 3rd and 4th Function Hosing), nominal width 62 inches, capable of both sideshift and fork-positioning functions.2.12 Hydraulic functions. Furnish all valves, controls, hydraulic lines, hoses, fittings, and other equipment required for complete operation of the fork-positioner and sideshift functions.2.13 Tires. Cushion tires, sized and load-rated by the manufacturer for the offered forklifts rated capacity and intended indoor operating surface with front tires: 28 inch x 16 inch x 22 inch (Cushion) and rear tires: 22 inch x 10 inch x 16 inch (Cushion).2.14 Steering. Full hydraulic power steering or functionally equivalent power steering with tilt steering column.2.15 Travel speed. Travel speed shall be not less than 4.8 miles per hour.2.16 Lift speed. Lift speed shall be not less than 32 feet per minute.2.17 Operator-presence protection. Furnish an operator-presence sensing system or equivalent safety interlock that prevents unintended vehicle movement or hydraulic operation when the operator is not properly positioned.2.18 Braking. Furnish a service-brake system and hand-actuated parking brake, or functionally equivalent parking-brake system.2.19 Warning devices. Furnish, at a minimum: (a) audible reverse alarm; (b) amber warning beacon/strobe; and (c) rear-facing blue warning light or equivalent visibility warning device.2.20 Rear visibility Furnish rear camera system or functionally equivalent rear-visibility aid.2.21 Lighting. Furnish forward work light(s) and rear combination light(s) suitable for normal indoor industrial operations.2.22 Operator display. Furnish an integrated operator display that includes, at a minimum, an hour meter and system-status information.2.23 Battery compartment. Forklift shall accommodate a battery compartment approximately 40 inches long x 60 inches wide, open-top configuration, or an equivalent configuration compatible with the offered forklift and required duty cycle.2.24 Battery and charger. Furnish forklift with compatible battery, charger, battery connector, and all charging accessories necessary for operation upon delivery.2.25 Warranty, complete forklift. Furnish a minimum warranty of 12 months or 2,000 operating hours, whichever occurs first, covering the complete forklift.2.26 Warranty, powertrain. Furnish a minimum powertrain warranty of 36 months or 6,000 operating hours, whichever occurs first.2.27 Manuals. Furnish one electronic and one hard-copy operators manual, maintenance manual, parts manual, and warranty documentation for each forklift.2.28 Delivery condition. Deliver forklifts fully assembled, serviced, inspected, and ready for operation.2.29 Operator orientation Provide on-site operator familiarization/orientation for Government personnel at time of delivery. Training shall address normal operation, safety features, charging requirements, daily inspection requirements, and basic preventive-maintenance actions.2.30 Compliance. The offered equipment shall comply with all applicable Federal, state, and local requirements for powered industrial trucks and workplace safety.2.31 Additional Equipment. Mechanical controls, Vinyl Semi-Susp. Seat, Operator Pres. Sens. Sys., Back-up Alarm, Rear Camera System Visibility Aid, Amber Strobe Light, Rear Facing Blue Light (Key Switch Activated), Gray SB350 Connector, Regenerative Braking, Full Hydraulic Power Steering, Hydraulic Multi-gauge, Operator Presence Sensing System (OPSS), Hand Actuated Disc Type Parking Brake, LED Headlight, Rear LED Combination Lights, Adjustable Vinyl Semi-Suspension Seat, Dual Operator Assist Grips, Hood Integrated Clipboard and Cup Holder, Durable Rubber Floor Mat, Heavy-Duty Planetary Drive Axle, Integrated Multi-Function Display w/Hour Meters, CAN-BUS interface.3. Manufacturer product literature, specification sheet, and dimensional drawing.3. A completed compliance matrix addressing each requirement in Section 2.4. Manufacturer documentation showing the forklifts rated capacity at the required:24-inch load center,103.5-inch maximum fork height, andfurnished fork and fork-positioner configuration.5. Description of the furnished battery, charger, connector, and charging accessories, if applicable.6. Warranty terms and authorized service-provider information.7. Proposed delivery schedule after receipt of order.Failure to provide sufficient documentation to establish compliance may render an offer ineligible for award.4. Inspection and Acceptance1. description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/SOURCES SOUGHT (SS) NOTIFICATION INCLUDING INDUSTRY FEEDBACK 1. Title: Independent Commissioning Agent (Owner�s Advocate) Services for U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases 2. Contracting Office: Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), R&D Contracting Division 1 - Branch 4 3. Location: Fort Detrick, Frederick, MD 4. Summary: This RFI/SS is issued solely for information and planning purposes and shall not be construed as a solicitation, restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach, or serve as an obligation on the part of the USAMRDC. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are advised that the United States Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI/SS will be solely at the interested responder�s expense. Not responding to this RFI/SS does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposal, if any is issued. No evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to Responders responding to this RFI/SS. The information resulting from this RFI/SS will determine interest and capabilities available in the marketplace; and will assist in developing acquisition strategy. 5. Background: The U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRIID), located at Fort Detrick, Maryland, is the premier lead medical research laboratory for the U.S. Department of War's biological defense research program. Since 1969, USAMRIID has provided leading edge medical capabilities to deter and defend against current and emerging biological threat agents. The Institute is the only laboratory in the Department of Defense equipped to safely study highly hazardous pathogens requiring maximum containment at Biosafety Level 4. USAMRIID has executed its mission from Building 1425. While historically significant, the legacy facility has surpassed its design lifespan. To sustain the DoD's biosafety integrity and research posture, the Department authorized the design and construction of a state-of-the-art replacement facility: Building 8100. Groundbreaking for the replacement complex took place in August 2009. In 2013, during the final construction execution and fit-out phases, Building 8100 experienced a fire that damaged critical mechanical, electrical, and plumbing infrastructure, Building Automation System controls, and associated laboratory boundary zones. Recovering from this event and achieving facility handover has become an acute operational hardship for the biodefense mission, delaying the transfer of ongoing medical research from the aging legacy facility. Note: Primary physical repair, mechanical completion, and prime construction execution are administered by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE). The Contractor shall not draft new architectural designs, stamp or seal engineering drawings, or execute physical facility redesigns. 6. Scope: The Government requires an independent, third-party technical Commissioning Agent (Owner's Advocate) to bridge the technical divide between USACE/prime construction execution and the stringent operational, biosafety, and regulatory compliance requirements of the end-user (USAMRDC Headquarters and USAMRIID). The Commissioning Agent will independently evaluate, witness, and verify critical facility systems and controls, and systematically advise the Government on executing a staggered/phased transition to achieve functional occupancy, biosafety accreditation, and facility registration. The formal closing date for this RFI/SS and for the submission of all responses is NLT 9 November 2026 at 12:00PM ET. All responses shall be submitted electronically using PDF or MS Word formats to the POC, Elizabeth O�Hara at elizabeth.m.ohara3.civ@health.mil. All responses received will be considered; however, a determination by the Government not to solicit the proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government reserves the right to continue market research and may issue additional RFIs if deemed necessary. Each response should include the following information and must not be more than fifteen (15) pages in length: Business Information: Company name, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone, website address (if available), and the name, telephone number, and e-mail address of a point of contact having the authority and knowledge to clarify responses with Government representatives. Unique Entity ID number, CAGE Code, and company structure (Corporation, LLC, partnership, joint venture, etc.). Companies also must be registered in System for Award Management (SAM, at www.sam.gov) to be considered as potential sources. Any and all Government Contracts/IDIQs (e.g. Federal Supply Schedule, OASIS+, etc.) you currently hold (to include the vehicle and your contract number) that could be used to fulfill this requirement. Do you or any proposed team members have an active role in the construction, controls, or installation for Building 8100? Please confirm your ability to certify organizational independence in accordance with FAR RFO 9.5. Technical Experience & Biocontainment Qualifications: Interested parties are requested to provide concise, direct responses to the following four (4) topic areas. General marketing literature is discouraged. BSL-3 and BSL-4 Containment Experience: Describe your firm�s specific experience serving as an independent Commissioning Agent or Owner�s Advocate on high- and maximum containment biological facilities (BSL-3, ABSL-3, BSL-4, ABSL-4). Highlight your experience with continuous negative pressure cascades, Bubble Tight Dampers (BTDs), APR doors, chemical suit shower skids and effluent decontamination systems. Regulatory Compliance Experience: Describe your firm�s past performance conducting comprehensive gap analyses, compiling Federal Select Agent Program (FSAP) registration packages (Biosafety, Security, Incident Response, BSAT Movement Plans under 42 CFR Part 73), verifying Tier 1 physical security layouts (minimum three physical barriers), and managing a live tracking register in secure environments. title: Lock, Key, and TRAKA Key Management Systems Maintenance and Support Services
description: The Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC), on behalf of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), is soliciting quotations for Lock, Key, and TRAKA Key Management System Maintenance and Support Services. This acquisition is a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS Code 561621 � Security Systems Services, with a corresponding small business size standard of $25 million in average annual receipts. Only responsible small business concerns that qualify as small under the applicable NAICS code and meet all solicitation requirements are eligible for award. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, management, materials, equipment, software licenses, technical support, and incidental services necessary to maintain FinCEN�s physical security and key-control systems. Services will be performed on an as-needed basis and may include preventive and corrective maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, replacement, installation, relocation, testing, configuration, software support, and emergency services. The systems and equipment covered by this requirement include TRAKA electronic key-management cabinets and associated software, Medeco high-security lock cores and related hardware, Kaba Mas X10 high-security locks, other high-security and manual door-locking hardware, and associated components, cabling, licenses, and ancillary equipment. The Government anticipates awarding a time-and-materials contract with an anticipated period of performance of five years, base period and four (4) option periods. The not-to-exceed (NTE) ceiling is $40,000 for each one-year contract period. If all four option periods are exercised, the maximum potential contract ceiling is $200,000. The Contractor must be a TRAKA-authorized reseller and installer and must possess an active, final Secret Facility Clearance (FCL) at the time of award. Offerors shall provide documentation demonstrating current TRAKA authorization and the capability to maintain, repair, install, and support FinCEN�s existing TRAKA, Medeco, Kaba Mas, Lockmasters, and associated locking systems, including applicable proprietary equipment, software, licensing, integration, and compatibility requirements. Contractor personnel performing services under the resulting contract must possess final Secret personnel security clearances before beginning performance and satisfy all applicable personnel-security, continuous vetting, and facility-access requirements identified in Section 7.0 of the Statement of Work. Interim facility and personnel security clearances will not be accepted. The Government will verify the required facility clearance prior to award and personnel clearance and access requirements prior to performance. Performance will occur at FinCEN facilities located in Washington, DC, and Vienna, Virginia.

title: Europe South District Playground Inspection, Maintenance, and Repair
description: The Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) is one of only two federally operated school systems in the United States. DoWEA plans, directs, coordinates, and manages pre-kindergarten through grade 12 educational programs on behalf of the Department of War (DoW). DoWEA operates approximately 165 brick-and-mortar schools across eight districts located in seven U.S. states, eleven foreign countries, Guam, and Puerto Rico, serving more than 72,000 students worldwide. DoWEA Europe consists of multiple districts encompassing schools, District Superintendent Offices (DSOs), and Student Transportation Offices (STOs) supporting children of active-duty military members and eligible civilian employees. The Contractor shall provide full-service, performance-based playground inspection, preventive maintenance, repair, emergency response, cleaning services for DoWEA facilities located in Europe South Region. For the purposes of this PWS, playgrounds include all playground systems and associated features, whether standalone or co-located, including but not limited to: Playground equipment and structures; Playground surfacing systems; Hard-surface and multi-use play courts; Outdoor recreational and athletic surfaces; and, Perimeter features, furnishings, and appurtenances. The Contractor shall furnish all management, supervision, labor, tools, equipment, materials, transportation, documentation, and incidentals necessary to ensure playgrounds remain safe, serviceable, compliant, and operational throughout the period of performance.
